prize_parts.citation: for the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, which made the synthesis of aryl amines general

statement.case_for: I moved my preferred configuration from B017 to B021. My first-round test was a clearly attributable discovery with mechanism-level content, independent confirmation and no crowded credit. After the exchange B021 meets that test better than my own candidate does. Somfai and Zou showed that C-N coupling is mechanistically distinct from the 2010 C-C reactions: the new elements are amine binding and deprotonation, suppression of beta-hydride elimination, and facilitation of the slow C-N reductive elimination through bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphine ligands. That is a mechanism-driven ligand design principle, which is the kind of argument I find persuasive. The method is about thirty years old, has been confirmed independently through several ligand and precatalyst generations, is used at process scale, and Buchwald and Hartwig are a clean pair. Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide chemistry is a precursor to name in the citation background, not a third seat.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize is still a real objection for Chabes and Aqvist, who read C-N coupling as an extension of an honoured framework, and I do not claim the question is closed. B021 is organometallic methodology, outside my own expertise, and my change of position rests partly on the failure of my own candidate to gain traction (no other member ranked B017 in the top eight at opening), so I should be cautious that I am not simply following the leaders. B017 remains scientifically sound, but it is conceptual, has no support beyond Chabes, Aqvist's remark and myself, and its priority picture does not change a vote count. Kosugi's priority also depends on chronology I cannot verify from the supplied material, and the expert reports should settle it.

responses.point: Somfai argues that the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling of organometallic nucleophiles, that C-N coupling needed its own ligand design, and that Kosugi belongs in the background of the citation, not on the laureate list.
responses.response: This answered my first-round objection. I had treated the 2010 prize as reducing urgency, but a different bond, a different bond-forming step and a different ligand problem make it a distinct achievement. I now agree with him on Kosugi and with the two-name allocation. I part from him only on B017: I do not claim it outranks a general method on impact, but it was not a weak candidate, and I keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: Zou states that the decisive new element is ligand design that overcame beta-hydride elimination and slow reductive elimination, and that thirty years of validation and no attribution dispute make B021 more secure than base editing or perovskites.
responses.response: This is the mechanistic statement the chair asked for, and it moved me. I would test it by asking the expert reports to confirm that the ligand-controlled catalytic cycle was established independently by both groups and that the stoichiometric tin chemistry did not already supply the principle. If it holds, B021 is the cleanest allocation on the shortlist. I agree with her that perovskites and base editing carry maturity or attribution questions that B021 does not.

responses.point: Chabes treats C-N coupling as an extension of an honoured field and ranked B017 fifth as a coherent experimental pair, below sequencing, lipid nanoparticles and degraders.
responses.response: I take the extension argument seriously, and it is the main reason I list B017 as an alternative and do not rank B021 above any doubt. My answer is that the new C-N mechanism, not the metal, is the achievement. I also see his point that Gray and Winkler is clean on credit but conceptual, and in this round I would not press it ahead of a method with comparable cleanliness and far broader reach.

responses.point: Aqvist says B021 may be an extension of Pd cross-coupling and asks whether ligand design is a new principle or a successful application of an existing one, which decides whether it displaces base editing for him. He also names Liu alone for B052.
responses.response: My answer is that the ligand problem is itself mechanistic: a different elementary step limits the reaction, and bulky electron-rich ligands were designed to address it. I agree that Liu is the clear principal on B052 and that Liu alone is better than a trainee-inclusive part, but the 2020 CRISPR prize and the short clinical record still make me hold base editing back. I welcome his willingness to revisit B021, and I thank him for the generous reading of Gray and Winkler.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the mechanistic distinction between C-N and C-C coupling or reads the 2010 prize as having covered the principle.
Whether Kosugi is correctly treated as a precursor; I rely on recollection of the chronology and the expert reports should confirm it.
Whether members who did not rank B017 would support it, which in round 1 looked unlikely and which this round did not change.
Whether my shift away from my own field reflects the evidence or a wish to join the leading candidates; I have tried to base it on the mechanistic argument only.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi, Gray or Winkler. My research on respiratory electron and proton transfer is scientifically close to B017 (the reason I earlier noted possible bias), which is proximity and not a recusal ground; I no longer prefer that candidate, which reduces the issue. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who has no tie to the credited names.
